promotionalText: Your in-laws, the stress at home—write it down without your name. Only empathy stamps come back, and posts disappear in 24 hours. It's okay to let it out.
description:
It's okay to let it out.

Kobosu is a place to write down what weighs on you at home—your in-laws, misunderstandings with your partner, the frustrations of parenting and housework—without using your name. The only thing that comes back is empathy stamps. Posts disappear automatically after 24 hours.

■ Three promises
• A place without names — No sign-up, no profiles, no followers. Nothing shows who wrote a post.
• Only empathy comes back — There's no comment section. You receive four stamps: "I get it," "That's rough," "Same here," and "You're doing great."
• Nothing stays behind — Posts disappear automatically after 24 hours. You can also delete them right away.

■ What you can do
• Listen: Filter by category—in-laws, partner, parenting, housework, money, your parents, siblings and relatives, caregiving, work and family, and more—and read how others feel. Each post shows how long until it disappears.
• Let it out: Write up to 400 characters. When Kobosu finds names, places, schools or workplaces, or phone numbers, you choose whether to mask them. Drafts stay on your device.
• Notes: See how many people said "Same here" to your posts, and the breakdown of stamps.
• App lock: Lock the app with Face ID or your passcode. Its contents stay hidden when you switch apps.
• Report and hide: Report a post anonymously by choosing one reason, or quietly step away with "Don't show this post."

■ For moments when
• You want to talk, but can't tell the people close to you
• You'd rather hear "I get it" than advice
• You want to write it down and feel a little lighter

"Delete all data" in Settings removes your shared posts, the empathy you sent, and your device's anonymous ID all at once.
